"""Money-talk detector for layer 15 MLP unit 2816 (down_proj component 2816).

About half of this component's variance comes from one MLP hidden unit (index 2816) that
reads the same direction; the rest is spread over many units. Its output direction
promotes "discount", "discounts", "tax", "deduction" and "concession" as next tokens, and
its activation is largest on words about discounts, prices, savings, tax, credit and loans
(e.g. " discount", " bulk", " savings", " tax", " offers", "优惠", "折扣").

The program scores each token by whether it is such a money word, and adds a decaying
memory of recent money words in the same document, so a run of deal-talk stays lit.
Everything else gets 0. It explains very little of the variance (about 0.2% on eval): most
of the activation, which is heavy-tailed and context-driven, is not carried by any word list.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MONEY_WORDS = frozenset(
    """discount discounts discounted deal deals save saves savings bargain cheap cheaper
    coupon coupons promo promotion sale bulk offer offers offered exclusive free deduction
    deductions tax taxes credit loan loans debt interest rebate refund price prices pricing
    financing funding eligible gift""".split()
)
MONEY_CHARS = "折优惠减免打税贷息低免費無料"
HIT_WEIGHT = 0.45  # activation for a money word itself
MEMORY_WEIGHT = 1.8  # weight on the decayed count of recent money words
MEMORY_DECAY = 0.95  # how fast the memory fades per token


def is_money(token: str) -> bool:
    word = token.strip().lower()
    return word in MONEY_WORDS or any(ch in MONEY_CHARS for ch in token)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    memory, last_doc = carry if carry is not None else (0.0, None)
    if doc != last_doc:
        memory = 0.0  # a new document starts with no memory
    hit = 1.0 if is_money(prefix.token_strings[-1]) else 0.0
    value = HIT_WEIGHT * hit + MEMORY_WEIGHT * memory
    memory = MEMORY_DECAY * memory + (1 - MEMORY_DECAY) * hit
    return (memory, doc), value

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 2817 (component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:2817).

The layer-15 MLP's down projection reads 6144 hidden units. This component reads one
direction that is almost entirely hidden unit 2817, so its activation is that unit's
value (scaled to about 1). What the unit responds to is mixed, and most of its variance
is not explained by words: this program captures the strongest word-level triggers only.

Predicted values (fit on 4096 training rows, about 0.5M tokens):
- +2.7 on programming sentinel words, with a leading space: " err", " nil", " None",
  " null", " bool", " True", " False", " undefined", " Exception", " Error", " ok", " ✓".
  These mark "something failed, or is empty or boolean" in code.
- +2.5 on citation brackets in papers: "[@", "][", "\\[".
- +1.7 on a digit right after an opening "[", as in "[3]".
- -1.1 on source-code words that start Python or Go lines: "from", "import", "func",
  "package", "Python", "python", " File".
- 0 everywhere else.
"""

READS = ()

SENTINELS = {
    " err", " nil", " None", " null", " bool", " True", " False",
    " undefined", " Exception", " Error", " ok", " ✓",
}
CITATION_BRACKETS = {"[@", "][", "\\["}
SOURCE_WORDS = {
    "from", "\tfunc", "func", "package", "import", "Python", " Python",
    "python", " python", "/python", " File",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if tok in SENTINELS:
        value = 2.7
    elif tok in CITATION_BRACKETS:
        value = 2.5
    elif tok.isdigit() and prev == "[":
        value = 1.7
    elif tok in SOURCE_WORDS:
        value = -1.1
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""Tool-call closing detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj:2818.

This component's activation is a dense, diffuse readout: most positions sit near
0.03 with spread about 0.33, and nothing in the text explains that spread well.
Its large negative values do concentrate in one place of an agent transcript: where
a tool call closes. The JSON arguments end with `"}}` and a newline, the tool call
ends with the `</tool_call>` tag, and the turn-end tokens right after that tag
(`<|im_end|>`, then a newline) stay negative. This program predicts those closing
positions as negative and every other position as the typical small value.
"""

READS = ()

TOOL_CLOSE = "</tool_call>"
ARGS_CLOSE = ('"}}\n', "}}\n")

TOOL_CLOSE_VALUE = -2.3
ARGS_CLOSE_VALUE = -1.9
AFTER_CLOSE_VALUE = -1.9
TYPICAL_VALUE = 0.03


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    recent = prefix.token_strings[-3:-1]  # the two tokens before this one
    if tok == TOOL_CLOSE:
        value = TOOL_CLOSE_VALUE
    elif tok in ARGS_CLOSE:
        value = ARGS_CLOSE_VALUE
    elif TOOL_CLOSE in recent:
        value = AFTER_CLOSE_VALUE
    else:
        value = TYPICAL_VALUE
    return carry, float(value)

"""Baseline for p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:2819.

This component's activation is a diffuse, context-dependent signal with no simple
token, position or repetition rule behind it (see the analysis notes). Its best
simple prediction is its typical value: a constant near its mean, -0.02.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.02


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Baseline program for layers.15.mlp.down_proj:2820.

What the component does: almost nothing that can be read off the text. Its
activation is dense, centred on about zero, with a standard deviation near 0.3,
but it never passes the causal-importance threshold (0 of 10M tokens), and
switching it off changes the model's next-token predictions by about 1e-6 nats.

What was checked on about 131k positions of training text:
- the token identity (a per-token mean) explains no held-out variance;
- coarse token classes (letters, digits, punctuation, whitespace, Han) and
  position in the document explain about 0.2% of the variance;
- whether the token already occurred earlier in the document, or the bigram
  was already seen, shifts the mean by less than 0.03;
- the only consistent-looking effect, a slightly positive mean after
  whitespace tokens, is not stable across rows and does not raise the score.

So the program predicts the component's mean activation at every position. It
explains none of the variance (it is the mean, not a pattern) and it leaves the
model's output essentially unchanged.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.0064


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 2821: a line-break detector.

On ordinary text this component sits slightly below zero. It switches up at line
breaks: a token that holds a newline (a plain line break, a blank line, or a
break glued to a colon or full stop), and also the two-character text backslash-n
that shows up in pasted, escaped text. Blank-line breaks are the strongest, then
breaks after a colon or full stop, then a single break. A bare colon or full stop
sits a little below the baseline.

Each value is the rounded mean activation of its class in the training data.
The program is stateless: it reads only the newest token. It explains only a
few percent of the variance (most of the component's activation is spread over
ordinary words, with no simple lexical pattern).
"""

READS = ()

BASELINE = -0.07  # words, digits, spaces, CJK text, most other tokens
PERIOD_OR_COLON = -0.25  # a bare "." or ":" (also the full-width forms)
ESCAPED_NEWLINE = 0.55  # the two characters backslash + n
ONE_NEWLINE = 0.35  # one line break, possibly with a colon or stop before it
BLANK_LINE = 0.8  # two or more line breaks in one token


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if tok.count("\n") >= 2:
        value = BLANK_LINE
    elif "\n" in tok:
        value = ONE_NEWLINE
    elif "\\n" in tok:
        value = ESCAPED_NEWLINE
    elif tok in (".", ":", "：", "。"):
        value = PERIOD_OR_COLON
    else:
        value = BASELINE
    return carry, float(value)

"""Token-class estimate of one MLP unit (layer 15, unit 2823) of Qwen3-1.7B.

The unit's output is silu(gate) * up. Its up-projection leans on the current
token's kind: number characters and capitalised name fragments push it up, plain
lowercase words push it down. The gate, which sets the size and sign, depends on
longer context this program cannot see, so the estimate is a small kind-based offset.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

WEIGHT_DIGIT = 0.17
WEIGHT_CAPITAL = 0.07
WEIGHT_LOWER = 0.01
BIAS = -0.03


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    value = BIAS
    if word and all(ch.isdigit() for ch in word):
        value += WEIGHT_DIGIT
    if word[:1].isupper():
        value += WEIGHT_CAPITAL
    if word.isalpha() and word.islower():
        value += WEIGHT_LOWER
    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 2824: a weak, diffuse feature.

What it does, in plain terms: it is a small signal spread over many tokens.
Its activation depends on context in ways no short rule captures: knowing the
current token's identity explains only about 4% of its variance, and the
rules below explain about 0.2%. The little structure there is:

- Capitalised words, acronyms and topical nouns (sports, food, events,
  everyday objects such as 'football', 'TV', 'cake', 'sales') sit a bit above
  the baseline.
- Lowercase adjectives ('national', 'local', 'modern', 'final') sit below it.
- Newlines and code punctuation sit a bit below it.

The program predicts the baseline plus these class offsets, using WordNet
for part of speech and semantic category. Everything else gets the baseline.
"""

import re

import wordnet

READS = ()

BASELINE = -0.033
TOPIC_NOUN_CATEGORIES = {
    "noun.food",
    "noun.process",
    "noun.event",
    "noun.phenomenon",
    "noun.artifact",
    "noun.act",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    value = BASELINE
    if re.fullmatch(r" ?[A-Z][a-z]+", token) or re.fullmatch(r" ?[A-Z]{2,}", token):
        value += 0.05
    if re.search(r"[_.()\[\]{};=<>]", token) or "\n" in token:
        value -= 0.02
    if re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]+", word):
        parts = wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)
        if parts and "adjective" in parts and "noun" not in parts:
            value -= 0.06
        elif parts and "noun" in parts:
            value -= 0.01
            if wordnet.categories(word) & TOPIC_NOUN_CATEGORIES:
                value += 0.09
    return carry, float(value)

"""Acronym-spelling-in-parentheses detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 2826.

This component is near zero almost everywhere, but it swings strongly negative on
the capital letters of an abbreviation spelled out inside an opening parenthesis:

    "... Provider of Services (POS"   "... Regional Infection Control Networks (IC"
    "... Ghana Institute of Management (G" + "IM"

The prediction depends on where the capital-letter token sits inside the parenthesis:

- the first capital-letter token after "(" is strongest when it is two letters
  ("(CP", "(RT": about -19), and moderately negative when it is one or three letters
  ("(S" before its continuation, "(POS": about -7); four or more letters: about 0;
- the second capital-letter token of the same parenthesis is about -9;
- the third is about -5; later ones are about 0.

Capitalised words such as "(Ali", and anything outside a parenthesis, are predicted 0.
The rule reads only the text so far, within the current document.
"""

import re

READS = ()

OPEN_PARENS = {"(", " (", "（"}
CAPS_TOKEN = re.compile(r"\s?[A-Z]{1,6}")
# predicted activation of the first capital-letter token after "(", by its letter count
FIRST_BY_LENGTH = {1: -7.0, 2: -19.0, 3: -7.5}
# later capital-letter tokens inside the same parenthesis, by how many came before
LATER = (-9.0, -5.0)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    # run: capital-letter tokens just before this one; opened: the token before that run is "("
    run, opened = (0, False) if carry is None or new_doc else carry
    value = 0.0
    if CAPS_TOKEN.fullmatch(tok):
        letters = len(tok.strip())
        if opened and run == 0:
            value = FIRST_BY_LENGTH.get(letters, 0.0)
        elif opened and run <= len(LATER):
            value = LATER[run - 1]
        run += 1
    else:
        run, opened = 0, tok in OPEN_PARENS
    return (run, opened), value

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 2827 (its down_proj component), as a short rule set.

What the unit does, in plain terms: it is near zero almost everywhere. Its large
values are rare and fall into a few recognisable places in text:

- Stack-trace frames. The word "at" that opens a line, as in Java or Node traces
  ("    at org.foo.Bar(...)"), gives a large positive value (about +7 on average).
- Package and URL name pieces in code, such as org, net, com, class, struct, link,
  test, http. These give a small positive value (about +1).
- "with" right after a design verb ("designed with your comfort in mind",
  "built with ..."). This gives a negative value (about -5).

Everywhere else the program predicts the unit's typical value, about +0.05.
Most of the unit's variance is a diffuse, context-driven spread of about 0.5 that
no token rule captures, so this program explains only a small share of it.
"""
READS = ()

DESIGN_VERBS = {"designed", "built", "made", "printed", "formatted", "redesigned"}
CODE_NAME_PIECES = {"org", "net", "com", "class", "struct", "link", "test", "http"}
TYPICAL = 0.05


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (only spaces so far on the current line, previous word); None at a row's start.
    at_line_start, prev_word = carry if carry else (True, "")
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()

    # Track whether the next token will be the first word on its line.
    if "\n" in token:
        line_start = token.split("\n")[-1].strip() == ""
    else:
        line_start = at_line_start and word == ""
    carry = (line_start, word)

    if word == "at" and at_line_start:
        return carry, 7.0
    if word == "with" and prev_word in DESIGN_VERBS:
        return carry, -5.0
    if word in CODE_NAME_PIECES:
        return carry, 1.0
    return carry, TYPICAL

"""Layer 15, MLP down_proj, component 2828: a "guarantee / assurance" word detector.

It fires on words that promise, warrant or certify something: "guarantee",
"WARRANTIES", "assure", "promise", "confidence", "bound", "proved", "rigorous".
Its output direction promotes next words of the same kind (guarantee, commit,
assure), so it is a feature for guarantee and assurance language.

The program gives each word group a typical activation. It also adds a weaker
bump on the one or two tokens right after such a word ("guarantee [on]",
"WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF [ANY]"), and predicts 0 for everything else.
Off those words the activation is weak and of mixed sign (spread about 0.5)
and follows the wider context, which a word list does not capture, so this
program explains under 1% of the component's variance. Its main value is the
word-level picture of what the component responds to.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# (word stems, typical activation); a token is matched by a stem inside its lowercased text
GROUPS = (
    (("guarant",), 5.0),
    (("warrant",), 3.0),
    (("assur", "promis", "pledg", "garant"), 1.7),
    (("confiden", "disclaim", "liabil", "merchantab"), 1.5),
    (("prove", "proof", "bound", "rigor", "precis", "accura", "certif"), 0.5),
)
AFTER = (0.4, 0.2)  # bump on the 1st and 2nd token after a guarantee word


def group_value(word):
    for stems, value in GROUPS:
        if any(stem in word for stem in stems):
            return value
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # carry: the group values of the previous two tokens of this document
    last, before = carry if carry is not None else (0.0, 0.0)
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        last, before = 0.0, 0.0
    own = group_value(prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower())
    value = own + AFTER[0] * (last > 0) + AFTER[1] * (before > 0)
    return (own, last), value

"""Inferential-conclusion connectives, written as a negative activation.

Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:2829 is mostly silent. It
goes strongly negative on a word that introduces a conclusion drawn from what
came before: "So", "Thus", "Therefore", "hence", "consequently", and lowercase
"so" used the same way (", so the ..."). It is near zero on other words,
including "then" in its time sense and "so that" for purpose. Almost all of its
variance outside those words is small token noise that this program does not
model.

The program looks at the newest token only. If it is one of the conclusion
words (ignoring case and leading space), it predicts a fixed value of -3.0 nats
of activation; everywhere else it predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

# Words that introduce a conclusion, as typed after a sentence or clause break.
CONCLUSION_WORDS = {"so", "thus", "therefore", "hence", "consequently"}

# Typical activation on such a word, from sampled training text (about -3 on average).
CONCLUSION_VALUE = -3.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    value = CONCLUSION_VALUE if word in CONCLUSION_WORDS else 0.0
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 2830: a mostly negative signal keyed to the current word.

In plain terms: the component is negative on the prepositions "in", "for", "on" and "at"
(most on "in"), on the object pronouns "it", "them" and "him", and on the same kind of
preposition in other languages ("en", "в", "на", "dans", ...). It is mildly negative on
"of", and mildly positive on forms of "be" and on "not", "also", "than", "from". Every
other token sits near the component's average, about -0.1.

The program reads only the newest token and looks it up in these word groups. It is a
word-level approximation and explains only a few percent of the variance: the activation
also depends on context (for example, which verb or noun comes before "in") that a word
list cannot capture.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Locative and temporal prepositions: the strongest negatives, "in" most of all.
PREPOSITION_VALUES = {"in": -1.0, "for": -0.8, "on": -0.5, "at": -0.5}
# Object pronouns and the same kind of preposition in other languages.
STRONG_NEGATIVE = {"it", "them", "him", "en", "в", "на", "dans", "für", "pour", "по", "для", "de"}
# Forms of "be", plus "not", "also", "than", "from": mildly positive.
MILD_POSITIVE = {"was", "be", "been", "are", "should", "not", "also", "than", "from"}
# Every other token sits near the component's average.
AVERAGE = -0.1


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word in PREPOSITION_VALUES:
        value = PREPOSITION_VALUES[word]
    elif word in STRONG_NEGATIVE:
        value = -0.85
    elif word == "of":
        value = -0.25
    elif word in MILD_POSITIVE:
        value = 0.15
    else:
        value = AVERAGE
    return carry, value

"""Baseline program for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 2831.

What the component does: its activation is (hidden . V_c) * ||U_c|| at each token. Over
training text it is a small, diffuse signal (mean about 0.03, std about 0.30), it never
passes the causal-importance threshold (0 of 10M tokens), and switching it off changes
the model's next-token predictions by about 1.5e-6 nats per position. Nothing in the
token prefix predicts it: token identity, the previous token, bigrams, and simple
character classes all explain no variance on held-out positions. So the honest
prediction is the component's typical value everywhere.

The program predicts that constant, the activation's mean over training text.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.03


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # Constant prediction: no token or position information helps.
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 2832, seen through its down-projection component.

This component's input direction is almost entirely that one MLP hidden unit (1.02 of
its 1.18 norm), so its activation tracks how strongly that unit fires. The unit is a
source-code signal. It is most positive on the end of a function or method header
(`func main()`, `def get_device()`, `void f()`) and on the closing ` */` of a doc
comment sitting above a declaration. It is negative in prose and markdown, where
`getAttribute()` is a mention of a call rather than a definition.

The rule set below scores each token by what it is, with weights fitted on training
rows. It explains only a few percent of the variance: most of the unit's activity is
small and diffuse, and depends on context these rules do not read.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Words that open a definition or declaration on a line.
DEF_WORDS = re.compile(
    r"\b(func|def|function|void|fn|public|private|protected|static|int|string|class|"
    r"sub|async|export|test|describe|it)\b"
)
# Tokens that begin a declaration or annotation.
DECL_TOKENS = {
    "public", "private", "protected", "void", "function", "def", "func", "fn",
    "static", "class", "return", "=>", "@", "int", "const",
}
# An empty call pair, as in `main()`, `(void)`, or `f()` followed by more text.
CALL_PAIR = re.compile(r"^\s?\(\)|^\(void")


def _line_before(prefix, limit=40):
    """The text of the current line before the newest token, within its document."""
    text = ""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    for i in range(len(prefix.token_strings) - 2, max(-1, len(prefix.token_strings) - limit - 2), -1):
        if prefix.document_ids[i] != doc:
            break
        piece = prefix.token_strings[i]
        if "\n" in piece:
            return piece[piece.rfind("\n") + 1:] + text
        text = piece + text
    return text


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if CALL_PAIR.match(token):
        # A `()` after a definition keyword closes a function header.
        return carry, 5.0 if DEF_WORDS.search(_line_before(prefix)) else 2.0
    if "*/" in token:
        return carry, 4.0
    if token.strip() in DECL_TOKENS:
        return carry, 0.7
    if "{" in token:
        return carry, 0.2
    if "`" in token:
        return carry, -0.2
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 2833: a near-constant, mostly unexplained readout.

What it does: predicts a small negative resting level almost everywhere, zero on the
first token of each document (where the component is silent), and a somewhat lower
level on the first few tokens of a document (positions 1-9).

Why so simple: over 8k training rows (4.2M tokens) this component has no token or
context trigger that a person could name. Token identity explains about 2% of its
variance (a full per-token table), a position rule about 0.1%, and token classes
(digits, punctuation, code, CJK, newlines) essentially nothing. It never passes the
causal-importance threshold (0 of 10M tokens), and switching it off barely changes the
model's predictions, so there is no circuit role to describe. The program captures the
coarse shape of its activation, not its variance.
"""

READS = ()

RESTING = -0.03  # typical activation in the middle of a document
EARLY = -0.1  # positions 1-9 of a document
EARLY_END = 10


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the current token's index within its document (None at the row's start).
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    new_doc = carry is None or len(docs) < 2 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]
    index = 0 if new_doc else carry + 1
    if index == 0:
        value = 0.0
    elif index < EARLY_END:
        value = EARLY
    else:
        value = RESTING
    return index, value

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 2834: a "keep it exactly as it is" detector.

What it does: this component's output direction pushes the next-token guess toward words
like "faithfully", "accurately", "exact", "original" and "full". Its activation is positive
on the words that say something should stay whole, literal or unmodified ("full", "entire",
"whole", "original", "exact", "exactly", "raw", "literal", "preserved", "as is"), on "as"
in "keep it as" or "make sure they are as expected", and mildly on shell-command words
("command", "execute", "bash", "run").

What it leaves out: the bulk of the activation is mild (about +/-0.5) and spread over
ordinary text and code with little link to any word list. On held-out text the current
token alone explains under 1% of its variance, and adding the previous token only about
3%, so this program captures only the spikes on those word classes and predicts 0
everywhere else. Its eval score is about 0.8% of variance explained.

Values are the mean activations measured on the training sample, one per group.
"""

READS = ()

# Words that say something stays whole, exact, literal, raw, original or unmodified.
WHOLE_OR_EXACT = {
    "exact", "exactly", "precise", "precisely", "literal", "literally", "strict", "strictly",
    "raw", "intact", "original", "full", "entire", "whole", "complete", "completely",
    "faithful", "faithfully", "verbatim", "unedited", "unchanged", "unmodified",
    "preserve", "preserved", "retain", "retained", "accurately", "identical", "pure", "plain",
    "actual", "direct", "directly", "simply", "correct", "correctly", "same",
}

# Shell and command words, where the component is mildly positive.
COMMAND_WORDS = {"command", "commands", "execute", "run", "bash", "df", "cat"}

# Words before "as" that make it mean "in the same state as before" ("keep it as", "are as expected").
KEEP_WORDS = {"keep", "kept", "keeps", "are", "is", "be", "it", "remain", "stay", "make", "sure"}

WHOLE_VALUE = 0.85
COMMAND_VALUE = 0.46
AS_VALUE = 2.5


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if word == "as" and same_doc and prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() in KEEP_WORDS:
        return carry, AS_VALUE
    if word in WHOLE_OR_EXACT:

"""Adult-content, gambling and ad-spam words, as a running density.

This component is mostly quiet. It goes negative in spam-like web text: pornography
and escort ads, online casinos and lotteries, and Chinese or Japanese keyword-stuffed
ad text (色情, 成人, 视频, 在线, 美女, 赌场 ...). It is most negative on such a word,
and stays somewhat negative for a while after, as the spam context builds up. Clean
prose and maths are near zero.

The program flags each word in the list, keeps a running density of flags in the
document (multiplied by DECAY at each step, reset at each new document), and predicts
a negative activation from the current flag and that density. Matching is on whole
words for English (so 'sexual' and 'updating' do not count) and on substrings for
Chinese terms.
"""

READS = ()

DECAY = 0.98     # how slowly the spam context fades
HIT = -1.5       # predicted activation for a flagged word itself
DENSITY = -0.6   # predicted activation per unit of running density

# English and other-language words, matched as whole words.
WHOLE = ("sex", "sexy", "sexe", "sexo", "porno", "porn", "dating", "slot", "slots",
         "online", "gratis", "zdarma")
# Stems matched at the start of a word: porn, escort, casino, erotic, gambling ...
STEMS = ("porn", "escort", "erot", "eskort", "casino", "gambl", "poker", "hentai",
         "nude", "xxx", "lesbian", "prostit", "viagra", "cialis", "lottery",
         "rencontre", "incontri", "massage", "sexo", "sexe", "sesso", "porr")
# Chinese and Japanese terms, matched anywhere in the token.
CJK = ("色情", "成人", "情趣", "黄色", "性感", "激情", "淫", "啪", "美女", "慰", "奶",
       "乳", "穴", "逼", "炮", "骚", "妻", "妇", "赌", "博彩", "棋牌", "彩票", "老虎机",
       "开户", "娱乐城", "在线", "视频", "免费", "高清", "下载", "网站", "官网", "直播",
       "图片", "小说", "影院", "电影", "亚洲", "国产", "主播")


def is_flagged(token):
    """True if the token (decoded alone) is a word from the lists above."""
    word = token.strip().lower()
    return (word in WHOLE or word.startswith(STEMS)
            or any(term in word for term in CJK))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """One position: flag the newest token, then predict from it and the running density."""
    density, doc = (0.0, None) if carry is None else carry
    doc_now = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if doc_now != doc:
        density = 0.0  # a new document starts a fresh context
    hit = 1.0 if is_flagged(prefix.token_strings[-1]) else 0.0
    density = DECAY * density + hit
    return (density, doc_now), HIT * hit + DENSITY * density

What it does: its activation is positive on the current word when that word names a
shortfall, failure or deviation from normal, the bad or extreme pole of a scale. It is
strongest on words like "missing", "lack", "failed", "invalid", "insufficient", "poor",
"empty" and "excessive", and of medium strength on "weak", "slow", "late", "low",
"negative", "decreased", "without" and "too". The opposite ends of such scales ("high",
"short", "hot", "double", "positive", "increased") and negation prefixes (un-, non-,
mis-) give a weaker positive value. Everything else, including "in", "with", "if" and
"both", predicts zero.

Why: the unit writes the word "or" (and its translations) into the output, and these
are the words that start "X or Y" contrasts of problems ("missing or invalid",
"too high or too low", "high or low"). The values are the mean activations per tier,
fitted on training rows; token identity explains only a small part of the activation.
"""

# Chinese words for the same ideas.
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"(missing|missed|misses|miss$|lack|fail|insuffic|inadequa|deficien|shortag|excess|"
    r"invalid|improper|incomplet|incorrect|wrong|faulty|defect|broken|malfunc|premature|"
    r"delay|forgot|overlook|empty|lost|unable|unauthori|abnormal|duplicat|unnecessar|"
    r"impaired|irregular|inconsisten|unstable|unsafe|unfair|unused|unwanted|leak|error|"
    r"null|undefined|illegal|poor|corrupt|flaw)"
)
CHINESE = ("缺", "失败", "错误", "不足", "过多", "不佳", "损坏", "故障", "漏", "不够", "违反",
           "低下", "非法", "过度", "缺乏")
# The bad or extreme pole of a scale, medium strength.
MEDIUM = {"weak", "slow", "late", "empty", "low", "negative", "decreased", "without", "too",
          "bad", "lower", "reduced", "limited", "difficult", "hard", "dry", "dead", "stuck",
          "loss", "less", "fewer", "over", "under", "increased", "cold", "worse"}
# The other pole, and negation prefixes, weak strength.
WEAK = {"high", "higher", "short", "hot", "double", "positive", "increase", "decrease",
        "small", "large", "long", "multiple", "off", "old", "non", "un", "mis", "no", "out",
        "down", "fast", "closed"}

STRONG_VALUE, MEDIUM_VALUE, WEAK_VALUE = 2.1, 0.9, 0.45


def activation_of(token: str) -> float:
    """The predicted activation for one token, from its tier."""
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if any(token.startswith(c) for c in CHINESE) or STRONG.match(word):
        return STRONG_VALUE
    if word in MEDIUM:
        return MEDIUM_VALUE
    if word in WEAK:

    return carry, activation_of(prefix.token_strings[-1])

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 2837: a diffuse signed feature with no simple trigger.

What we measured (16k training rows, about 8.4M tokens):
- Its activation is roughly symmetric around zero: mean +0.05, std 0.35, range about -2 to +2.
  It is almost never important to the output (causal importance is about 0 everywhere).
- It is not a token detector. Per-token means explain under 2% of its variance on held-out
  text, and token surface classes (digits, punctuation, capitalised words, non-ASCII) differ
  by less than 0.05. Previous-token and bigram lookups add nothing, and neither do document
  topic or rolling counts of token classes.
- The one clean structure: the first token of every document (and of every packed row) gives
  an activation of about 0, while every later token has mean +0.05.

So this program predicts the average activation everywhere except at a document's first
token, where it predicts 0. That captures the one real regularity; it explains essentially none
of the remaining variance, which no short rule we found accounts for.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Average activation at ordinary tokens (measured on training rows).
MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.05


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # A document starts at the row's first token, and wherever the document label changes.
    doc = prefix.document_ids
    starts_document = len(doc) == 1 or doc[-1] != doc[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if starts_document else MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Comma-in-enumeration detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 2838.

This component is almost a single MLP hidden unit of layer 15 (its input direction
is ~99% that unit). Its activation is small and noisy almost everywhere. The one
readable thing it does is fire on the commas of a list, mainly when the list has
already started and the item just finished is a short enumerator such as a number
or a letter (`1, 2, 3,` or `A, B, C,`). Commas that close a longer item, such as a
name or a phrase, fire weakly. The first comma of a line (only one item so far)
stays near zero. Every other token predicts 0.

The program keeps, per line, the text of the item being typed and how many commas
the line has had. It resets at each newline and at each new document.
"""

READS = ()

SHORT_ITEM = 2  # an item of at most this many characters is a short enumerator
SHORT_VALUE = 2.0  # predicted activation at a comma closing a short enumerator
LONG_VALUE = 0.25  # predicted activation at a comma closing a longer item


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    item, commas = carry if carry is not None else ("", 0)
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    if len(ids) > 1 and ids[-1] != ids[-2]:
        item, commas = "", 0
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if "\n" in tok:
        return ("", 0), 0.0
    if tok.strip() == ",":
        if commas == 0:
            value = 0.0
        elif len(item.strip()) <= SHORT_ITEM:
            value = SHORT_VALUE
        else:
            value = LONG_VALUE
        return ("", commas + 1), value
    return (item + tok, commas), 0.0

What it is: this rank-one piece reads the layer-15 MLP hidden units, mainly unit 2840
(+) and unit 3454 (-), and writes a tiny vector into the residual stream. Its activation
is a small, mostly negative, noise-like value (mean about -0.065, std 0.27) that changes
from token to token. Token identity, the previous token, token class, position, and
model entropy explain almost none of it (at most about 2% of the variance in tests).

What this program does: predicts the typical value, -0.065, at ordinary positions, and 0
at the first token of a row or of a new document, where the component is always ~0
(std 0.001 there). It does not try to predict the token-to-token variation, which no
simple rule captures.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

TYPICAL = -0.065  # the component's typical activation at ordinary positions


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    starts_document = prefix.position == 0 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if starts_document else TYPICAL

"""Baseline for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 2841.

This component is a weak, diffuse direction: its activation has mean about 0.08 and
spread about 0.3, but nothing a reader can name predicts it. Token identity, the
previous token, the bag of recent tokens and the in-document position together explain
almost none of its variance (held-out R^2 about 0.01 at best). Its effect on the model
is negligible too: switching it off moves next-token predictions by about 2e-6 nats.

So this program predicts only the one visible regularity: the activation is near zero
at the first tokens of a document and drifts up to about 0.09 as the document goes on
(roughly by log2 of the position, flat after about 128 tokens). Position resets at each
document boundary, as the model's attention does.
"""

import math
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

PEAK = 0.09  # typical level once a document is well under way
RAMP_START = 4  # log2 of the position where the rise begins (16 tokens in)
RAMP_LEN = 3  # log2 span of the rise (reaches PEAK at 128 tokens)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # carry: (document label, index of the document's first token), or None at a row start.
    t = prefix.position
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        start = t
    else:
        start = carry[1]
    n = t - start  # position within the current document
    if n < 1:
        value = 0.0
    else:
        frac = (math.log2(n) - RAMP_START) / RAMP_LEN
        value = PEAK * min(1.0, max(0.0, frac))
    return (doc, start), value

"""Clause-boundary unit: layers.15.mlp.down_proj, unit 2842 of Qwen3-1.7B.

What the unit does, in plain terms: it is high on punctuation that closes a clause,
where the next thing is a new clause or a connective. The strongest case is the comma
ending an opening clause such as "If you are unsure, ..." or "Since 2010, ...": the
main clause is about to start. Full stops and question marks are also fairly high.
Commas between short list items ("hardware, showers, toilets") are weak.

It is negative on the discourse connectives themselves ("However", "Therefore",
"Thus", "Wait", "Furthermore"), which open a new clause rather than close one. Other
words sit near zero, and the unit is not well explained by any word identity.

The program keeps three facts from the text so far: the document (reset at a new
document), the first word of the current sentence, and how many words have passed
since the last comma or sentence end.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words that open a subordinate or introductory clause: a comma after them closes it.
OPENERS = {
    "if", "when", "whenever", "although", "though", "since", "because", "once",
    "while", "as", "after", "before", "where", "unless", "until", "whether", "despite",
}
# Discourse connectives and transition adverbs: they open a new clause.
CONNECTIVES = {
    "however", "therefore", "thus", "hence", "furthermore", "moreover", "consequently",
    "accordingly", "additionally", "similarly", "whereas", "wait", "actually",
    "basically", "sometimes", "usually", "typically", "always", "especially",
    "particularly", "specifically", "finally", "eventually", "initially",
}
COMMAS = {",", "，", "、"}
SENTENCE_ENDS = {".", "!", "?", "。", "！", "？"}

# Typical activation by case (fitted on sampled training rows, see explanation).
OPENER_COMMA = 1.5
LIST_COMMA = 0.5
CLAUSE_COMMA = 1.0
SENTENCE_END = 0.8
OTHER_PUNCT = 0.2
CONNECTIVE = -0.5
PLAIN_WORD = 0.05


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = tok.strip().lower()
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    # carry: (document id, first word of this sentence, words since last comma or end)
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, None, 0)
    _, first, seg = carry

    if tok in COMMAS:
        if first in OPENERS:
            value = OPENER_COMMA
        elif seg <= 2:
            value = LIST_COMMA
        else:
            value = CLAUSE_COMMA
        seg = 0
    elif tok in SENTENCE_ENDS:
        value = SENTENCE_END
        first, seg = None, 0
    elif not tok.strip():
        value = OTHER_PUNCT if "\n" in tok else PLAIN_WORD
        if "\n" in tok:
            first, seg = None, 0
    elif not any(ch.isalnum() for ch in tok):
        value = OTHER_PUNCT
        seg += 1
    else:
        value = CONNECTIVE if word in CONNECTIVES else PLAIN_WORD
        seg += 1
        if first is None:
            first = word
    return (doc, first, seg), float(value)

"""Judgement-context detector for layer 15's MLP hidden unit 2845 (negative = "is this right?" talk).

The component reads almost only one MLP hidden unit (about 70% of its input weight is on unit
2845), so its activation is roughly that unit's value times the norm of its output column. The
unit is mostly quiet, and dips negative in text that judges correctness, certainty or approval:
"correct", "make sure", "verify", "as expected", "I am happy with", "wrong", "yes". The dip
spreads a little past the word itself, so a run of such words keeps it low for a few tokens.
This word-list version explains only a small share of the variance: most of the unit's
variation is not tied to any words.

The program scores each token by how judgement-laden its word is (strong words -1, milder
ones -0.4, others 0), keeps a fading average of that score over the document so far, and
predicts a weighted sum of the two. Documents reset its memory, as the model's attention does.
"""

READS = ()

# Strong judgement words: correctness, error, approval.
STRONG = set("""correct correctly correctness incorrect wrong verify verified happy pleased
proud glad satisfied thrilled""".split())

# Milder judgement words: certainty, expectation, agreement, checking.
MILD = set("""sure expected check checked necessary yes think believe fine good valid ready final
consistent sufficient error mistake mistakes decision decisions accurate accuracy confirm okay
agree reasonable convinced certain confident seems indeed""".split())

DECAY = 0.7  # how fast the document's judgement memory fades per token
W_TOKEN = 1.4  # weight of the current word's score
W_MEMORY = 1.7  # weight of the faded memory of earlier words


def word_score(text):
    """-1 for a strong judgement word, -0.4 for a milder one, 0 otherwise."""
    word = text.strip().lower()
    if word in STRONG:
        return -1.0
    if word in MILD:
        return -0.4
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if carry is None or len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        memory = 0.0
    else:
        memory = carry
    score = word_score(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    value = W_TOKEN * score + W_MEMORY * memory
    new_memory = DECAY * memory + (1 - DECAY) * score
    return new_memory, value

What it does: it is silent (about 0) at the first token of each document, and
elsewhere it sits at its typical small negative value (about -0.019, the mean
over sampled training positions). Its activation has spread about 0.44 around
that mean, and that spread does not follow the current token, the previous
token, the token's character class, whether the token repeats earlier in the
document, or where it sits in the document. So this program predicts the
mean and explains essentially none of the variance; the measured
variance explained is about zero.

Why: the component's contribution is tiny (about 0.7% of its site's output
RMS), and switching it off changes the model's next-token predictions by
almost nothing. Nothing readable in the tokens predicts its size or sign.

TYPICAL = -0.019


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):

    first = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if first else TYPICAL

What it is: a dense, roughly symmetric signal (sd about 0.45) that is almost unrelated to the
text. Switched off, it changes the model's next-token predictions by about 3e-6 nats per

(that unit carries about 70% of its variance). The unit itself is diffuse: no token table or

- The first token of each document is zero.

    " against", " between", " over", " under", " around", " inside", " outside", " beyond",
    " near", " via",

    " the", " a", " an", " both", " either", " each", " other", " various", " two", " this",

    if token in DETERMINERS and previous in OTHER_PREPOSITIONS:

    if token.strip().isdigit():

    # the last WINDOW + 1 tokens' words, None where they belong to an earlier document

    for i in range(max(0, len(ids) - WINDOW - 1), len(ids)):

    if word in PRONOUNS:
        value -= 0.3
    value += 0.3 * min(sum(1 for w in before if w in MATH), 2)
    return carry, value

The component is almost exactly one MLP neuron of layer 15: its read direction is
dominated by unit 2879, which carries about 40% of its variance by itself. Most of the
time it is near zero. It has three clear tilts:

- Chinese text: the full-width comma "，" is high (about 0.9, higher inside poems
  and lyrics), other commas and line ends are moderately high, and the Chinese full
  stop "。" and "；" are negative (about -0.3).
- Poetry and song writing: once a document mentions a poem, verse, rhyme, lyrics,
  a limerick or a chorus, commas go up (ASCII commas about 0.2 outside Chinese, 1.0
  inside it), and ordinary tokens in Chinese verse go up a little.
- Everything else (code, maths, tool output, ordinary prose) is near zero or slightly
  negative.

The program tracks two things as it reads: whether the recent text is Chinese (at
least 30% of the last 16 tokens of the document contain a Han character), and whether
a poetry word has appeared so far in the document (carried forward, reset at each new
document). Its prediction is the average activation for the matching cell. It explains
only a little of the variance, because most of the activation is small, unstructured
noise; the table is what a readable rule can get.

import regex

READS = ()

HAN = regex.compile(r"\p{Han}")
POETRY = regex.compile(
    r"(?i)poem|poetry|verse|rhym|lyric|\bsong|limerick|sonnet|haiku|ballad|stanza|chorus"
    r"|poesia|poème|poésie|gedicht|诗|歌词|押韵|韵脚"
)
WINDOW = 16
TAIL = 40
STOPS = {"。", "；", "。”"}


def in_chinese_text(prefix):
    """True if at least 30% of the last WINDOW tokens of this document contain a Han character."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    lo = max(0, len(prefix.token_ids) - WINDOW)
    recent = [
        s for s, d in zip(prefix.token_strings[lo:], prefix.document_ids[lo:]) if d == doc
    ]
    return sum(bool(HAN.search(s)) for s in recent) / len(recent) >= 0.3


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    poetic, tail = (False, "") if carry is None or new_doc else carry
    tail = (tail + tok)[-TAIL:]
    poetic = poetic or bool(POETRY.search(tail))
    zh = in_chinese_text(prefix)
    if tok == "，":
        value = (1.8 if poetic else 0.93) if zh else (0.3 if poetic else 0.46)
    elif "," in tok:
        value = (1.0 if poetic else 0.73) if zh else (0.24 if poetic else 0.03)
    elif "\n" in tok:
        value = (0.9 if poetic else 0.05) if zh else (0.12 if poetic else 0.05)
    elif tok in STOPS:
        value = -0.3 if zh else -0.04
    else:
        value = (0.2 if poetic else 0.04) if zh else (0.04 if poetic else 0.013)
    return (poetic, tail), float(value)
